summary: Quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for Brightnote's site search. Covered embeddings endpoint, similarity search patterns, re-ranker endpoint and how to stitch in post-retrieval reranking, console walkthrough for routes and instrumentation, and Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization. Customer concerned about latency and data residency; asked for pricing and security docs. Agreed on POC scope and next steps.
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jamie Chen, AE on the Redwood team. With me is Luis Martinez, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Aisha (Brightnote): Hi Jamie, thanks. Good to be here. We got Tom and Maya on as well.
[00:10] Tom (Brightnote): Hey. Morning.
[00:12] Maya (Brightnote): Hello.
[00:14] Luis (Redwood SE): Great, quick agenda — we’ll do a short discovery, then a live walkthrough of the hosted embeddings endpoint, then the reranker/demo pattern, and finish with Q&A and next steps.
[00:23] Aisha: Sounds good. Our main goals are improving search relevance on content and reducing query latency. Right now we use Elastic + some vector store. We saw Redwood's benchmarks and wanted to see how embeddings + rerank flow would work.
[00:35] Jamie: Perfect. Can you give a bit on traffic and SLA needs? e.g., queries per second, p95 target?
[00:40] Tom: We're around ~200 QPS at peak on the docs site, p95 latency target is 200-250ms end-to-end. Also multi-tenant index per customer is important; data residency for EU customers is a requirement.
[00:52] Luis: Cool. Two things I’ll call out early: with the hosted API you can route EU traffic to EU regions and we provide audit logs + KMS integration for enterprise plans. For latency, we usually see embeddings + rerank patterns in the 80-200ms range depending on model and network.
[01:08] Maya: When you say rerank, is that a separate endpoint or do you do it in one shot?
[01:12] Luis: It’s typically a two-step flow: first retrieve candidates via dense/sparse retrieval — you can use our embeddings endpoint to vectorize and store vectors in your store, or we can host vector index partner integrations — then we call the reranker endpoint which takes candidate docs + query and returns scores or rewritten results. It lets you use a smaller general model for retrieval and a tuned reranker for quality.
[01:28] Jamie: I’ll demo a simple cURL and then show the console.
[01:32] [00:32] (start screen share)
[01:34] Luis: Alright, first the embeddings call. Example payload: POST /v1/embeddings with model: redwood-search-v1, text: query text. Response returns a 1536-d vector. You can store this in your vector DB. Quick note — our auto-batching helps if you send many upserts.
[01:50] Aisha: Does the hosted API do any prefix caching or KV cache for embeddings?
[01:54] Luis: Good question — embeddings are deterministic per model+input so you can cache on your side. For text generation we have KV cache for decoding; for embeddings we recommend either a TTL cache or store vectors in your DB. Our Optimize tool will suggest caching/batching settings based on traffic.
[02:10] Tom: What's the typical vector dimension for your models and do you support quantized vectors?
[02:15] Luis: Most of our search-optimized models use 1536-d; we also support 1024-d variants. For storage, quantized vectors are handled by your vector store. On the inference side we support quantized model runtimes for cost saving but that's orthogonal to the stored vector format.
[02:29] [02:30] Jamie: Now the reranker demo. I'll show a simple flow: retrieve top-K by vector similarity (we'll pretend the vector DB returns some doc ids and snippets), then call POST /v1/rerank with query and candidates.
[02:40] (typing)
[02:42] Luis: Notice the reranker accepts candidate context array and returns scores; you can also request a subdoc highlight. We handle streaming tokens for long contexts but for rerank it's usually synchronous.
[02:54] Aisha: Can the reranker be constrained by an allowlist or SSO? We need to ensure it doesn't surface PII.
[03:00] Luis: We have content filters and allow you to add guardrails client-side. For PII, we recommend redaction at ingestion; we also provide enterprise data retention controls and support for customer-managed keys.
[03:12] Maya: On the cost side, how should we think about reranker vs retrieval costs?
[03:17] Jamie: Typically retrieval is cheap (vector similarity + DB cost), embeddings incur per-vector cost on inference, reranker is per-candidate scored — so reranking K=10 will be more expensive than K=3. Optimize can recommend K and batching depending on your latency vs cost sweet spot.
[03:33] Tom: We're sensitive to p95; if reranker adds 80ms, that might push us. Can you do lightweight reranks or fallbacks?
[03:40] Luis: Yes — you can use a smaller, faster reranker model. Also Redwood supports a tiered routing policy: hot low-latency model for prioritized users and a cost-optimized fallback model. If latency SLO is missed we can auto-fallback.
[03:53] Aisha: Show us the console for routes and tracing.
[03:56] [04:00] (switch to console)
[04:02] Luis: Here’s the Routes page — you can create a route that maps /search to a model+policy, enable rate limits and circuit breakers. The tracing tab shows token-level latency and per-request traces; you can filter by model, route, or customer token.
[04:18] Maya: Can we see cost breakdown per token?
[04:20] Luis: Yes, billing -> usage breakdown shows token counts, embeddings vs generation costs, and per-route cost attribution. We also expose a cost simulator for projected monthly spend given QPS and K.
[04:33] Tom: Is there an existing Algolia/Pinecone connector or do we do custom integration?
[04:37] Luis: We have out-of-the-box connectors for Pinecone and a generic vector store good for Elastic + kNN. For Algolia you'd typically use their custom ranking with external vectors; we can share integration notes.
[04:48] Aisha: On security, can we bring our own KMS and get SOC 2 artifacts?
[04:52] Jamie: Yes — enterprise/private plans support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS integrations) and we provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO artifacts under an NDA. We'll send the security pack link after the call.
[05:05] Maya: For the POC, we want EU residency for EU tenants. Are region pins available?
[05:10] Luis: Absolutely — you can pin routes to eu-west regions and we support private deployment for full on-prem if needed. For hosted we also support region-specific deployments and routing.
[05:19] [05:30] (demo of reranker response)
[05:22] Luis: Example response: [{doc_id: 123, score: 0.92, highlight: "..."}, ...] — apologies transcript shows braces but it's JSON in the console.
[05:31] Aisha: What about A/B testing and rollouts?
[05:34] Jamie: The console supports rollout policies — canary, percentage-based, and automatic rollback if quality regressions are detected via eval sets. You can tie quality alerts to prompt sets.
[05:45] Tom: For our use-case we need deterministic embeddings to avoid drift between reindex jobs. How do you handle model updates?
[05:51] Luis: Model versions are pinned per route; when we onboard a new model we provide a migration path and shadow tests. Also Optimize will suggest quantization/profile upgrades but we never auto-upgrade a pinned route.
[06:04] Aisha: Could you run a small benchmark against our sample dataset?
[06:07] Jamie: Yes — that’s the POC we usually do. Luis, we can run end-to-end: embed a subset, run retrieval+rerank latency tests, and produce cost/latency tradeoff spreadsheet.
[06:18] Luis: I'll own the benchmark sheet. For the POC we typically do 10k queries and measure p50/p95/p99 and unit cost.
[06:26] Maya: How long does POC usually take?
[06:28] Jamie: Typically 2-4 weeks depending on dataset and integrations.
[06:32] [06:30] (Aisha asks about long-term storage)
[06:33] Aisha: How long are logs retained and can we export traces?
[06:36] Luis: We keep standard logs 90 days, longer retention is available as an add-on. You can export traces to your SIEM or S3 for long-term retention.
[06:46] Tom: Any limits on candidate context length for reranker? We sometimes pass 8-10kb snippets.
[06:50] Luis: Reranker supports multi-kb contexts; for very long contexts we chunk and do streaming scoring. Keep in mind that longer context increases latency and cost.
[07:02] Maya: Do you have a recommended K for product docs search?
[07:05] Luis: For product docs we often recommend K=5-10 then rerank. Using K=3 is common for low-latency scenarios. Optimize will recommend based on your query distribution.
[07:15] Aisha: Could you share sample code for embeddings + rerank in node/python?
[07:18] Jamie: Yes, I'll attach SDK snippets. We have Node and Python examples in the docs; I'll include a minimal flow: embed -> upsert -> query -> rerank.
[07:28] [07:30] (brief silence as Jamie pastes links)
[07:33] Jamie: I posted links in the chat: security pack (link: https://redwood.ai/security), docs (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/search), and benchmark template (link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/template).
[07:45] Tom: Nice. About pricing — are embeddings billed per vector + token? Do you have tiered discounts?
[07:50] Jamie: Embeddings are billed per unit (per call) and reranks per candidate token scoring. We do tiered discounts for committed usage and Dedicated/Private pricing is different (reserved capacity). I'll send a sample pricing spreadsheet.
[08:01] Maya: For our legal team we'll need DPA + data processing terms.
[08:04] Jamie: We'll include the DPA and standard clauses in the security pack; legal can sign NDA if needed.
[08:10] Aisha: Any gotchas for integrating with our existing Elastic cluster? We want to avoid migrating everything.
[08:14] Luis: You can do hybrid: continue using Elastic for inverted indices and use our embeddings to augment results. We have scripts to bulk-upsert vectors into Elastic's kNN or Pinecone if you use that. The retrieval step can combine sparse + dense signals.
[08:28] Tom: Latency wise do you recommend co-locating vector store near Redwood region?
[08:31] Luis: Yes, network hop matters. If your vector DB is in the same cloud region we'll see lower latency. For hosted vector stores we can recommend partners with colocated options.
[08:43] Maya: Okay, what's the formal POC scope?
[08:45] Jamie: Proposed: 2-week POC; 10k queries; measure p50/p95/p99; evaluate relevance lift vs current Elastic baseline; provide cost/latency spreadsheet and recommended K and model. We'll also test region routing for EU tenants.
[08:57] Aisha: That works. We'll provide a sample dataset and evaluation queries by 2027-01-05.
[09:02] Luis: Great. I'll need API keys and a small allowlist IP or token to ingest vectors. We'll share a secure upload method in the benchmark doc.
[09:12] [09:30] (wrap-up)
[09:14] Jamie: Quick recap: Jamie send pricing + SDK snippets + security pack, Luis send benchmark template and run initial tests, Brightnote to provide dataset + queries. Schedule POC kickoff week of Jan 10. Anything else?
[09:26] Tom: No that's all. Thanks.
[09:28] Aisha: Thanks everyone.
[09:30] Jamie: Thanks — we'll follow up via email with notes and the jira/ticket.
notes: Demo included live reranker POST /v1/rerank example and console walkthrough for routes/tracing.
Customer priorities: p95 latency 200-250ms, EU data residency, multi-tenant indices.
Agreed POC: 2 weeks, 10k queries, evaluate relevance vs Elastic baseline.
